s.g: Combining form used to form imperfective counterparts of prefixed derivatives of со́хнуть (sóxnutʹ, “to dry (intransitive), to wither”).

ety.text: From imperfective lengthening of the Proto-Slavic perfective infinitive stem *-sъx- (from the infinitive *sъxnǫti) + -а́ть (-átʹ). Similar lengthening accounts for the change -о- → -а- in imperfective derivations in -ывать (-yvatʹ) and -ивать (-ivatʹ), e.g. * осмотре́ть pf (osmotrétʹ, “to examine”) → осма́тривать impf (osmátrivatʹ), * отбро́сить pf (otbrósitʹ, “to throw away”) → отбра́сывать impf (otbrásyvatʹ), * приколо́ть pf (prikolótʹ, “to pin”) → прика́лывать impf (prikályvatʹ).

s.g: Assyrian Neo-Aramaic language, a Neo-Aramaic dialect of Modern Aramaic

ety.text: Borrowed from Turkish bakkal, from Arabic بَقَّال (baqqāl).

ety.text: From the Old East Slavic безмьздьнꙑи (bezmĭzdĭnyi). By surface analysis, без- (bez-) + мзда (mzda) + -ный (-nyj).

From ма́тер- (máter-) + -ный (-nyj), based on the oblique stem of мать (matʹ, “mother”); compare мат (mat, “obscene language”), derived from the same word.

ety.text: From при- (pri-) + вере́дливый (verédlivyj, “weak, effeminate”), from ве́ред (véred, “boil, abscess”) + -ливый (-livyj), where ве́ред (véred) originally meant, and still dialectally means, "pain, harm"; compare doublet вред (vred). Sense development "too sensitive to pain" → "weak, effeminate" → "squeamish, picky".

Inherited from Old East Slavic притъча (pritŭča, “incident”), from Proto-Slavic *pritъča (“incident, tale”). The meaning "tale" is likely a semantic loan from Old Church Slavonic притъча (pritŭča, “tale, parable”).

ety.text: Thought to be from пядь (pjadʹ, “span; Russian unit”) + -ица (-ica, feminine agent suffix), drawing a parallel to English geometer moth and translingual Geometra.

ety.text: From пять (pjatʹ, “five”) + -и- (-i-) + гора́ (gorá, “mountain”) + -ск (-sk), referring to the nearby Mount Beshtau in the northern Caucasus.
